note: Section 5.2 step 3b: "(No SAs are created in response to receipt of a packet that requires IPsec protection; only BYPASS or DISCARD cache entries can be created this way.) If there is no match, discard the traffic." Re-judged 2026-11-08 (independent auditor) after bf2e2d753c and 652591fc76 changed apply.go::applyConfig, releaseSPD and unmatched_xfrm_interface.go::installXFRMInterfaceEntries. applyConfig: on the first apply the node catch-all still goes in first (installUnmatched), then applyApplicationOverride (the RFC4301-4.4.1-8 setsockopt guard), then the IKE bypass; a refused guard returns with the catch-all in force and nothing else installed. On a reload the guard and the interface entries move ahead of every SPD change, so a refusal leaves the running SPD as it was. releaseSPD only adds a deferred releaseApplicationOverride after the catch-all leaves; the guard is no SPD entry, so the catch-all is still the last SPD entry removed and is still kept when warnSPDLeft reports a leftover. installXFRMInterfaceEntries now returns an error naming the interface when its catch-all is refused, skips that interface's if_id 0 exemptions in the same pass, and applyConfig returns that error after the prune: an interface SPD without its final entry is no longer reported applied. The two gap paths are unchanged: vppPolicyInterface and defaultDataplaneSource are byte-identical, so VPP still installs no catch-all (unmatched bypass only) and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 manual-key entries still have none beneath them; on either path an inbound packet matching no entry is delivered. Unimplemented stands. The prior annotation finding (an interface catch-all refusal only logged) is resolved by bf2e2d753c, and the {gap} text now names it with TestInterfaceSPDCatchAllInstallFailureFailsTheApply; its claims (catch-all first, IKE bypass after, catch-all removed last and kept on a failed removal) still hold over the new code. {gap} annotation accurate. Re-judged 2026-11-10 after the gocritic rangeValCopy fix moved the fingerprints of unmatched.go::installUnmatched and unmatched_xfrm_interface.go::installXFRMInterfaceEntries: installUnmatched now ranges over the catch-all policies by index and passes *p to InstallPolicy, the same values in the same order with the same error return; installXFRMInterfaceEntries ranges over a map that holds *xfrmInterfaceEntry instead of the value, and no entry is mutated after planXFRMInterfaceEntries builds it, so the role order, the held and guarded skips, the per-interface noFinalEntry refusal, the InstallPolicy(entry.params) call and the recorded set are unchanged. Nothing these functions enforce moved, and no other cited producer or annotation changed; the verdict below stands on the same reading.
